skillator-pending.run.gemini:
!{sh "{{SKILLS}}/tickets-zordon/scripts/pending.sh"}

Above is the output of tickets-zordon's pending script for this repo. Paste it to me unchanged; it reads, it never edits the board.

skillator-update.profile.antigravity: This command is shared by Codex, Antigravity CLI, Antigravity IDE and Gemini CLI. Each loads its own copy from its own skills directory, so the profile in step 1 is the invoking CLI's. Target host by the CLI running it: Codex -> `codex`; Antigravity CLI -> `agy`; Antigravity IDE -> `antigravity`; Gemini CLI -> `gemini`. This copy's location should agree: `.gemini/antigravity-cli/skills` is agy's, `.gemini/config/skills` the Antigravity IDE's, `.gemini/skills` Gemini CLI's, and the `skills` directory of a Codex home Codex's. If they disagree, or the invoking CLI cannot be told, ask before running any installer.

skillator-update.records.all:
1. This copy was written into the skills directory `{{SKILLS}}`, so its profile is that directory's parent, `{{SKILLS}}/..`. Use that parent, as a plain absolute path without `..`, as `<profile>` - never another CLI's or profile's directory. Choose `<host>` as the host-specific instructions above say. If the CLI running this command does not own that profile, or the host is ambiguous, ask. Never infer the active host from another CLI's environment variables. Report the chosen host and profile before updating.
2. Before pulling anything, note the installed version from the profile itself: the one line in `{{SKILLS}}/.skillator-version` (the installer writes it beside the source pointer). If that file is missing (an install older than this record), read the `version` in `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` of the directory named in the source pointer `{{SKILLS}}/.skillator-source`, now, before any pull. Otherwise the installed version is `unknown`.
3. Resolve the source - the first of these that exists, and say which: a. the optional checkout path; b. the directory named in the source pointer from step 2, if it still holds both installers; skip a pointer whose path contains `/.skillator-update-source` or `\.skillator-update-source` (this command's own private checkout, used only as c.); c. the dedicated checkout `<profile>/.skillator-update-source`, cloning the Skillator marketplace repository, `https://github.com/bodish-coder/skillator.git`, there when it is missing. Resolve the installer directory: the selected source itself if it holds both `install.sh` and `install.ps1`, otherwise its `plugin/` child if that holds both; neither -> report and stop. Retain it as `<src>`. Run `git -C <src> rev-parse --show-toplevel` to detect checkout membership, including a plugin subdirectory or linked worktree whose `.git` is a file. Success -> use its output as `<checkout-root>` and run `git -C <checkout-root> pull --ff-only`. Pull fails (diverged, dirty, no upstream): never merge, reset, stash or force. From a. or c. -> report it and stop before installation. From b. the pointer is a hint, not an order -> say the pull failed and go on to c. A confirmed nongit cache from a. proceeds without pulling; from b. it is skipped for c.; missing Git or any other lookup error -> report and stop, not a cache fallback. Only for the dedicated checkout `<profile>/.skillator-update-source`, after the pull: verify HEAD equals its upstream and that it has no local changes; either check fails -> report and stop. A clone the user owns (a. or b.) needs only the successful fast-forward pull. Re-check both installers in the retained `<src>` after pulling; either missing -> report and stop. Do not infer that an old plugin cache is current.
4. After the pull, read the `version` in `<src>/.claude-plugin/plugin.json`. Compare it with the installed version from step 2 as dotted numbers. Lower than the installed version -> refuse: report both versions and stop before installing - never a downgrade. Installed version `unknown` -> say so and continue.
5. Windows: `powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File "<src>/install.ps1" -Force -TargetHost "<host>" -TargetProfile "<profile>"`. Other platforms: `sh "<src>/install.sh" --force --target-host "<host>" --target-profile "<profile>"`. Pass both arguments, even for a default profile. On failure stop and report it.
6. Report the verified host, profile, and old and new versions (use "unknown" for an unavailable old version). Restart the current CLI to load the new files.

gauntlet-plan.plan-format.all: On this host /gauntlet-run reads it as data ("Run without the Workflow tool"), never executes it.

gauntlet-plan.plan-end.cursor: - on this host with the Task tool, one Task per agent.
gauntlet-plan.plan-end.pi: - on this host with the subagent extension when installed, else the phases in order in this session.
gauntlet-plan.plan-end.opencode: - on this host with the phases in order in this session (no delegate verified here).
gauntlet-plan.plan-end.antigravity: - on this host with agy: background subagents; codex: subagents; Gemini CLI: in this session.
gauntlet-plan.plan-end.gemini: - on this host with the phases in order in this session (no delegate verified here).

gauntlet-run.execution.all: the plan. The `.workflow.js` is read as data (`meta.phases`, `PLAN`), never executed.

gauntlet-run.dispatch.cursor: , driver `@cu-<6>`, `--owner task`) before the agent that runs it exists
gauntlet-run.dispatch.pi: , driver `@pi-<6>`, `--owner subagent` with the subagent extension, else `--owner session`) before its work starts
gauntlet-run.dispatch.opencode: , driver `@oc-<6>`, `--owner session`) before its work starts
gauntlet-run.dispatch.antigravity: ; agy: driver `@agy-<6>`, `--owner subagent`; codex: driver `@cx-<6>`, `--owner subagent`; Gemini CLI: driver `@gm-<6>`, `--owner session`) before its work starts
gauntlet-run.dispatch.gemini: , driver `@gm-<6>`, `--owner session`) before its work starts

gauntlet-run.parallel.cursor: A phase's tickets run at once through the Task tool, so the mode is the phase shape.
gauntlet-run.parallel.pi: With the subagent extension a phase's tickets run at once, so the mode is the phase shape. Otherwise in this session a phase's tickets run one after another - a parallel plan runs serial here, say so in the first line.
gauntlet-run.parallel.opencode: In this session a phase's tickets run one after another - a parallel plan runs serial here, say so in the first line.
gauntlet-run.parallel.antigravity: On agy/codex a phase's tickets run at once through subagents, so the mode is the phase shape. On Gemini CLI a phase's tickets run one after another - a parallel plan runs serial here, say so in the first line.
gauntlet-run.parallel.gemini: In this session a phase's tickets run one after another - a parallel plan runs serial here, say so in the first line.

gauntlet-run.delegate.cursor: , through the Task tool, one Task per agent (a phase's tickets as several Task calls in one turn)
gauntlet-run.delegate.pi: , through the subagent extension when installed, else in this session - the stored prompt done, then the verify text done as a second pass that edits nothing
gauntlet-run.delegate.opencode: , in this session (no delegate verified here) - the stored prompt done, then the verify text done as a second pass that edits nothing
gauntlet-run.delegate.antigravity: - agy: background subagents; codex: subagents (one subagent per ticket of the phase); Gemini CLI: in this session (no delegate verified there), the stored prompt done, then the verify text done as a second pass that edits nothing
gauntlet-run.delegate.gemini: , in this session (no delegate verified here) - the stored prompt done, then the verify text done as a second pass that edits nothing

skillator-ops.execution.opencode:
If the argument is `terminal` (or `--open`):
Open the ops board in a new terminal tab. From the repo root, run on Windows:
`powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File "{{SKILLS}}/ops-board/ops/ops.ps1" -Repo <repo root> -Open`
elsewhere:
`sh "{{SKILLS}}/ops-board/ops/ops.sh" <repo root> --open`
Then say one line: where it opened, or the error it printed. It reads; it never edits the board.

Otherwise (bare `/skillator-ops`, or a tab name like `tickets`, `workflows`, `health`, `messages`, `explorer`, `build`):
Display the ops board frame right here in the opencode app. From the repo root, run on Windows:
`powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File "{{SKILLS}}/ops-board/ops/ops.ps1" -Repo <repo root> --once $ARGUMENTS`
elsewhere:
`sh "{{SKILLS}}/ops-board/ops/ops.sh" <repo root> --once $ARGUMENTS`
Paste what it outputs, unchanged. It reads; it never edits the board.
